messages:
sam-devex: Heads-up — reproducible issue with JS SDK + function-calling + json_mode. Python client accepts the structured response but JS ends up failing schema validation. Minimal repro below.

sam-devex: ```js
// responses.create with function call + json mode
const res = await client.responses.create({
  input: 'create order',
  json_mode: true,
  function_call: { name: 'order.create', arguments_schema: orderSchema }
})
console.log(res.output)
```

sam-devex: Error we see (JS): `ValidationError: output mismatch: expected object but got string` — the output printed looks like a JSON string instead of an object: `"{\"items\":[...] }"`. Python SDK returns an actual object.

mike-ml: @sam-devex can you paste the raw response body from the JS SDK (before any app-level parsing)? curious if JS client is stringifying somewhere. :thinking:

sam-devex: pasted raw: `{"choices":[{"message":{"content":{"type":"output_structured","value":"{\"items\":[{\"id\":1}]}"}}}]}` — so we appear to be double-encoding the structured payload on the wire for JS.

jen-sdk: this rings a bell — JS client used a stringify step to preserve function argument fidelity in older browsers. we ended up `JSON.stringify`-ing structured outputs in a helper so `value` can sometimes be a string. Python leaves it as an object.

jen-sdk: quick fix options: (1) SDK-side: auto-detect and parse JSON strings when `json_mode=true`; (2) runtime-side: normalize so the response always uses native JSON types; (3) provide a small helper e.g. `sdkHelpers.parseJsonMode(output)` so apps opt-in.

alex-runtime: runtime should be consistent but we intentionally left some backward compat shims. that said, if we're going to keep those shims we should annotate the payload with `encoded_as_string: true` or similar so SDKs can handle deterministically. current behavior is brittle.

ben-engineer: +1 to a compatibility flag. also propose adding a validator helper: `validateStructuredOutput(schema, output, { coerceJsonStrings: true })` so customers can opt to coerce string->json for schema checks.

mike-ml: also worth checking retry/auth layers — if a retry replays already-stringified body we might double-stringify. has anyone confirmed whether this happens only on first attempt or also on retries?

sam-devex: I ran it with retries disabled, still reproduced. looks like the SDK transform is the culprit (JS-only).

jen-sdk: I'll open a tiny patch to the JS client that parses JSON strings when `json_mode` is set and includes a unit test. will also expose `sdkHelpers.parseJsonMode` and `sdkHelpers.validateStructuredOutput`.

sam-devex: thanks — can you also add a sample-app test case? failing sample app was `redwood/sample-apps` demo checkout that uses function calling and expects structured response. I'll open the PR to update the sample and add e2e.

sam-devex: PRs: https://github.com/redwood/sample-apps/pull/512 (sample fix + test) and https://github.com/redwood/js-sdk/pull/1043 (parse helper + tests)

ben-engineer: for the short-term patch we should add telemetry so we can see how often outputs are strings vs objects — add a `x-sdk-jsonmode-encoding: string|object` header or emit an event. helps quantify impact.

alex-runtime: agree on telemetry. if SDKs ship the patch we'll still normalize in runtime for new responses. I'll open a runtime ticket to mark payloads and remove shims after 2 releases.

ci-bot: deploy scheduled: js-sdk/docs-backports v0.12.3 -> staging at 2026-03-22T02:00Z (no prod deploy yet)

sam-devex: Action items: @jen-sdk patch JS SDK to parse JSON-strings, add sdkHelpers and validateStructuredOutput; @ben-engineer add telemetry; @alex-runtime create runtime ticket for payload annotation + deprecation schedule; I'll update sample-apps PR and follow up with QA.

mike-ml: great — please add a short note in the release notes and a snippet in the onboarding guide about `json_mode` quirks so integrators know what to expect.

sam-devex: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
